action: Farmers and USDA partners: expect intermittent outages of USDA payment tools; AgWeb says USDA expects most FSA programs to be running by end of business Friday. Use official USDA channels for updates.
date_note: Date is the Nextgov report; the internal disclosure was earlier that week (an email sent Monday).
exec: A US federal agency that pays farmers has taken applications offline after a security incident; who was responsible is not yet known.
plain: The US Department of Agriculture had a security incident and took several systems offline, including tools used to pay farmers. An official says no data was lost; who did it is not yet known.

sources.name: ABC Color (EFE, relaying NBC News), 20 Nov 2026

summary: Nextgov reports, citing anonymous sources and internal notices, that USDA applications were taken offline after a security incident. AgWeb quotes Under Secretary Richard Fordyce describing "limited outages" and no data lost. EFE, relaying NBC News, says attackers reached a platform used to process payments to farmers and that Fordyce confirmed a cyber threat to NBC. Responsibility is unresolved.
title: USDA takes multiple systems offline after internal security incident

validation.note: Nextgov/FCW (anonymous sources) originates the report; AgWeb relays it with on-record remarks by Fordyce; EFE relays NBC News, which separately reports the intrusion and Fordyce's confirmation to NBC (NBC's own page not read). Kept single_source until NBC's page is read.

review.note: Checked against Nextgov/FCW and AgWeb: facts, Fordyce remarks, no actor, single_source all match. Fixed occurred_at (Nextgov published 4:42pm ET = 21:42Z, was 20:42Z) and action (removed unsourced status tools and email-verification advice; added AgWeb Friday expectation).
